howBytesWereMeasured: sha256sum over files on disk and `git cat-file blob <commit>:<path> | sha256sum` for historical bytes. theRenderModeTrap: Sidestepped rather than survived. A lane that renders -gray -png on this poppler build gets mode=RGB and a naive read of it is silently wrong; there is no PNG here for that to happen to.

theFeeRuleGuard.questionAsked: FIX146 asked this lane to re-derive that feeRuleWithoutTheTrackSentence() can fail, because a guard that cannot fail proves nothing.
theFeeRuleGuard.answer: IT CAN FAIL, and it is stronger than FIX146 described it. Re-derived two ways, independently of FIX146's account.
theFeeRuleGuard.correctionToFIX146sOwnReport: FIX146 says the function "asserts the removal three ways" and that it proved three mutations. The function carries FOUR assertions: (1) the routing sentence is present; (2) no "this track" survives its removal; (3) the Article 983(A) cap still heads what remains; (4) what remains ends on /Article 983\(G\)\.$/. FIX146 named and proved the first three and did not name the fourth. This lane proved all four.
theFeeRuleGuard.unitLevel: Eight inputs through the exported feeRuleWithoutTheTrackSentence(), committed at tools/fee-rule-guard-mutations.mjs. The unmutated committed value returns 846 characters and does not throw. Seven mutations -- sentence deleted; sentence reworded 'this track'->'this pathway'; a SECOND 'this track' inserted before the known sentence; the cap sentence deleted; the cap reworded 'caps'->'limits'; the 983(G) tail deleted; a sentence appended after the routing sentence -- each throw, and each throws from the limb it targets. 8 of 8 behaved as predicted.
theFeeRuleGuard.integrationLevel: Four surgical mutations were written to data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, each touching ONLY the tracks[179].rules.fees value (the routing sentence occurs THREE times in that file -- also at packetSet.participantActionRequired[17].description and packetSet.requiredBeforeFiling[17] -- so a whole-file replace would have mutated three fields and proved less). The build was run against each. ALL FOUR STOPPED THE BUILD with exit 1, and under none of them did a single fixture byte get written.
theFeeRuleGuard.theOneRefinementThATMATTERS: Of the four, three stop INSIDE the guard (build script lines 1133, 1135, 1137). The fourth -- deleting the routing sentence -- never reaches the guard: it is caught earlier, at loadAuthorityBinding, scripts/build-census-v1-la-976-arrest-no-conviction-set.mjs:298, by assert.match(registryTrack.rules.fees, /very often available on this track/i). So the guard's own limb 1 is unreachable through the build path and is live only at unit level. The build still stops, which is what matters; but 'three mutations each stopped the build' and 'three limbs of this guard fired' are not the same statement, and only the first is true.
theFeeRuleGuard.scopeLimit: The guard covers tracks[179].rules.fees alone. The same routing sentence sits in two other fields of the same track. Neither reaches a filed page today -- this lane's scan finds no routing vocabulary on filed pages 1-8 -- but nothing guards them if a later edit routes one to a filed page.
